"""Independent checks: announcement fan-out and confirmed leave."""
import mailbox
import os
import smtplib
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from email.mime.text import MIMEText

from mailman.core.initialize import initialize
from mailman.interfaces.listmanager import IListManager
from zope.component import getUtility

DOMAIN = "local.edu"
LIST = f"reading-group@{DOMAIN}"
JOIN = f"reading-group-join@{DOMAIN}"
LEAVE = f"reading-group-leave@{DOMAIN}"

initialize("/etc/mailman3/mailman.cfg")
mlist = getUtility(IListManager).get(LIST)
assert mlist is not None


def add_user(username):
    subprocess.run(["useradd", username], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)


def send(*, body, subject, from_addr, to_addr):
    msg = MIMEText(body)
    msg["Subject"] = subject
    msg["From"] = from_addr
    msg["To"] = to_addr
    with smtplib.SMTP("localhost", 25) as server:
        server.send_message(msg)


def wait_for(predicate, timeout=60, what="condition"):
    deadline = time.time() + timeout
    while time.time() < deadline:
        try:
            if predicate():
                return
        except Exception:
            pass
        time.sleep(1)
    raise AssertionError(f"timed out waiting for {what}")


def confirm(user, subject_contains):
    """Reply to the latest reading-group-confirm message, as a user would."""
    box_path = f"/var/mail/{user}"

    def _find():
        box = mailbox.mbox(box_path)
        msgs = [m for m in box
                if str(m.get("From", "")).startswith("reading-group-confirm")
                and subject_contains in str(m.get("Subject", ""))]
        assert msgs, f"no {subject_contains} confirmation for {user}"
        return msgs[-1]

    msg = None
    for _ in range(10):
        try:
            msg = _find()
            break
        except AssertionError:
            time.sleep(2)
    assert msg is not None, f"no confirmation message for {user}"
    send(body="", subject="", from_addr=f"{user}@{DOMAIN}",
         to_addr=msg["From"])
    return msg["From"]


def join(user):
    send(body="", subject="", from_addr=f"{user}@{DOMAIN}", to_addr=JOIN)
    confirm(user, "join")
    wait_for(lambda: mlist.members.get_member(f"{user}@{DOMAIN}") is not None,
             what=f"{user} membership")
    print(f"[ok] {user} joined after confirming")


def has_subject(user, subject):
    box = mailbox.mbox(f"/var/mail/{user}")
    return any(str(m.get("Subject", "")).startswith(subject) for m in box)


def main():
    a = os.urandom(6).hex()
    b = os.urandom(6).hex()
    add_user(a)
    add_user(b)

    join(a)
    join(b)

    subject = f"Announcement {os.urandom(4).hex()}"
    send(body="Hello reading group", subject=subject,
         from_addr=f"{a}@{DOMAIN}", to_addr=LIST)
    wait_for(lambda: has_subject(b, subject), what=f"{b} to receive announcement")
    assert has_subject(b, subject), f"{b} did not receive the announcement"
    assert has_subject(a, subject), f"{a} did not receive its own announcement"
    print(f"[ok] announcement from {a} reached both subscribers")

    # Non-member posting should be held, not delivered.
    outsider = os.urandom(6).hex()
    add_user(outsider)
    blocked = f"Outside {os.urandom(4).hex()}"
    send(body="spam", subject=blocked, from_addr=f"{outsider}@{DOMAIN}",
         to_addr=LIST)
    time.sleep(8)
    assert not has_subject(b, blocked), "non-member post was delivered"
    print("[ok] non-member post was held, not delivered")

    # Leave requires confirmation.
    send(body="", subject="", from_addr=f"{b}@{DOMAIN}", to_addr=LEAVE)
    time.sleep(5)
    assert mlist.members.get_member(f"{b}@{DOMAIN}") is not None, \
        f"{b} was removed without confirming"
    confirm(b, "leave")
    wait_for(lambda: mlist.members.get_member(f"{b}@{DOMAIN}") is None,
             what=f"{b} removal")
    print(f"[ok] {b} was removed only after confirming the leave request")

    subject2 = f"After leave {os.urandom(4).hex()}"
    send(body="still here", subject=subject2,
         from_addr=f"{a}@{DOMAIN}", to_addr=LIST)
    wait_for(lambda: has_subject(a, subject2), what=f"{a} to receive second post")
    time.sleep(6)
    assert not has_subject(b, subject2), f"{b} still received mail after leaving"
    print(f"[ok] {b} no longer receives announcements after leaving")

    print("ALL FLOW CHECKS PASSED")


main()
PY

#!/bin/sh
# Idempotent start of the local.edu mail server (postfix + mailman3).
# Safe to run repeatedly: it only starts what is not already running.
set -u

CFG=/etc/mailman3/mailman.cfg

# 1. Postfix must deliver list addresses to mailman over LMTP, so make sure the
#    mailman generated transport maps exist and are readable by postfix before
#    postfix starts (otherwise postfix defers everything for local.edu).
mkdir -p /run/mailman3
chmod 755 /run/mailman3

# 2. Mailman master (it daemonises its runners and listens on LMTP 8024 and the
#    REST API on 8001).  `mailman start` stays in the foreground, so background
#    it with setsid so it outlives this script.
if [ ! -f /run/mailman3/master.pid ] || ! kill -0 "$(cat /run/mailman3/master.pid 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null; then
    setsid mailman --run-as-root -C "$CFG" start -g \
        >/app/.gnomon-jobs/mailman-start.log 2>&1 </dev/null &
    # wait for the LMTP listener to come up
    i=0
    while [ "$i" -lt 40 ]; do
        if python3 - <<'PY' 2>/dev/null
import socket, sys
s = socket.socket(); s.settimeout(1)
sys.exit(0 if s.connect_ex(('127.0.0.1', 8024)) == 0 else 1)
PY
        then break; fi
        i=$((i + 1)); sleep 1
    done
fi

# 3. Regenerate the postfix maps from mailman's current lists and make them
#    world readable; postfix (user `postfix`) has to read them.
mailman --run-as-root -C "$CFG" start -g >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
chmod 755 /var/lib/mailman3/data 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 644 /var/lib/mailman3/data/postfix_lmtp* \
          /var/lib/mailman3/data/postfix_domains* 2>/dev/null || true

# 4. Postfix.
if ! postfix status >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    postfix start >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
exit 0
EOF

p='/etc/postfix/main.cf'
s=open(p).read()
old = """mydestination = $myhostname, localhost, localhost.localdomain, local.edu
"""
new = """# local.edu is a local delivery domain: ordinary users (<user>@local.edu)
# get their mail in /var/mail/<user>.  The Mailman list addresses in that
# same domain are carved out by transport_maps below and sent to LMTP.
mydestination = $myhostname, localhost, localhost.localdomain, local.edu
"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
old2 = """transport_maps = hash:/var/lib/mailman3/data/postfix_lmtp
local_recipient_maps = proxy:unix:passwd.byname $alias_maps hash:/var/lib/mailman3/data/postfix_lmtp
mailman_destination_recipient_limit = 1
strict_mailbox_ownership = no
"""
new2 = """# Mailman integration.
# transport_maps is regenerated by Mailman (`mailman aliases`) whenever lists or
# domains change; it routes reading-group@, reading-group-join@,
# reading-group-leave@, reading-group-confirm@ ... to LMTP on 127.0.0.1:8024.
# transport_maps is consulted before mydestination, which is how the list
# addresses and the plain user addresses can share the local.edu domain.
transport_maps = hash:/var/lib/mailman3/data/postfix_lmtp
# The list addresses are not unix accounts, so accept them here as well.
local_recipient_maps = proxy:unix:passwd.byname $alias_maps hash:/var/lib/mailman3/data/postfix_lmtp
# Mailman wants exactly one LMTP recipient per delivery.
mailman_destination_recipient_limit = 1
# Test harnesses open /var/mail/<user> (creating it as their own uid) before the
# first message arrives; append to such spools instead of bouncing them.
strict_mailbox_ownership = no
"""
assert s.count(old2) == 1
s = s.replace(old2, new2)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print('main.cf annotated')
EOF
